name: Saint Catherine of Siena
history: A dyer’s daughter of Siena, a Dominican tertiary who never learned to write well, yet counselled popes and princes, made peace between cities and urged the Pope to return from Avignon to Rome. Her Dialogue and her letters make her one of the great teachers of the Church. She is a Doctor of the Church and a patron of Europe and Italy.
life: Caterina Benincasa was one of the youngest of more than twenty children of a dyer and his wife Lapa. As a girl she gave herself to Christ and resisted every plan for her marriage. At about sixteen she joined the Mantellate, Dominican laywomen who lived at home, and spent three years in near silence in a small room of her father’s house. Then she went out to nurse the sick and serve the poor, above all in the plague of 1374, and a circle of disciples gathered round her, among them Blessed Raymond of Capua, her confessor. She received the stigmata at Pisa in 1375, visible to no one. In 1376 she went to Avignon and urged Gregory XI to return to Rome, which he did. When the Great Schism broke out she supported Urban VI and spent herself praying for the unity of the Church. She died in Rome, aged thirty-three.
prayerTo: Saint Catherine, you loved Christ crucified and His Church with a fire that the whole world felt. Pray for the Pope, for the unity and renewal of the Church, and for Europe. Help me to dwell in the cell of self-knowledge, and to speak the truth with courage and love. Amen.
penance: Pray today for the Pope and for the unity of the Church. Catherine fasted hard, but she also nursed the sick: visit or help someone who is ill.
meditation: She taught that we must build a cell of self-knowledge within the soul, and there find both our own nothingness and the goodness of God. Where is your inner cell?
